name: Le Méridien Ile Maurice
positioning: Beach resort in Pointe aux Piments, near Grand Bay in the north of Mauritius, on a kilometre-long beachfront with an adults-only wing called Nirvana
best_for: Families who want a kids club and a separate club for toddlers
Couples who want an adults-only wing with its own pool, bar and restaurant
Guests who want complimentary non-motorized watersports on the lagoon

facts.text: The resort is set in Pointe aux Piments, Mauritius.
The resort is located near Grand Bay in the north of Mauritius.
The rooms stretch along a kilometre-long beachfront with direct beach access.
Most rooms open onto lagoon-view balconies or terraces, and select rooms face lush gardens.
Butler service is provided in Royal Suites and Nirvana Suites.
Explore Spa is run in partnership with Phytomer, with treatments that focus on natural and organic ingredients and are based on Ayurveda.
The spa has a Snow Room inspired by Northern European traditions.
Le Méridien Family Kids Club is an indoor and outdoor secured playground for children aged 4 to 12.
Le Petit Club is designed for children aged 2 to 4.
The resort has floodlit clay tennis courts.
Jade serves dishes inspired by the flavours of Japan, Thailand and Cambodia.

highlights.text: Nirvana is an adults-only retreat by the lagoon, set apart in its own wing with a dedicated reception, a pool bar, an infinity pool and its own restaurant.
Plunge Pool Hideaway Suites on the ground floor open onto private courtyards with a hidden plunge pool.
Nirvana guests are welcomed with a bottle of wine, fresh fruit and floral touches in the room, and Nirvana hosts cocktails and canapés at sunset every day.
Water activities include stand-up paddleboarding, water-skiing, HobbyCat sailing and guided snorkel tours.
Memory Makers activities include family cooking classes and storytelling around a beach bonfire.

considerations.text: Sir Seewoosagur Ramgoolam International Airport is about 60.4 km from the hotel.
WhataHotel notes premium pricing reflecting the luxury positioning.
WhataHotel notes the remote island location requires international travel planning.
